title: MIT BoltzGen: Open-Source All-Atom Generative Model Designs Nanomolar Binders Across Proteins, Peptides, and Small Molecules
aiSystem: BoltzGen (Unified All-Atom Diffusion & Structure Model, MIT Jameel Clinic)
whyItMatters: Open-sourced by MIT’s Jameel Clinic, BoltzGen unified structure prediction and all-atom generative design in one model—achieving nanomolar wet-lab binders on 66% of nine novel therapeutic targets across proteins, nanobodies, and peptides.
summary: Released by MIT CSAIL and the Abdul Latif Jameel Clinic in October–November 2025 (bioRxiv / PubMed PMID 41394589), Hannes Stärk, Regina Barzilay, Tommi Jaakkola, and collaborators introduced BoltzGen, an open-source all-atom generative model that unifies biomolecular structure prediction and de novo binder design inside a single diffusion architecture. Unlike earlier backbone-only protein generators, BoltzGen natively designs binders across modalities—proteins, nanobodies, cyclic peptides, and small-molecule interfaces—while jointly modeling full atomic side chains and covalent constraints. Across nine challenging novel targets with no prior structural binders, testing only ~15 designs per target yielded nanomolar-affinity wet-lab binders for 66% of targets.
technicalHighlights: Unifies all-atom biomolecular structure prediction and multi-modal binder generation (proteins, nanobodies, peptides, small-molecule targets) in one open-source model.
Achieved nanomolar-level experimental binding affinity on 66% of nine novel, hard-to-drug targets with tiny wet-lab screening budgets (~15 designs each).
Released fully open-source under MIT’s Boltz ecosystem, catalyzing rapid 2026 follow-ons (BoltzProt-1, BoltzMol-1).
caveats: Validated experimentally across diverse academic and partner wet labs in the bioRxiv preprint (updated June 2026), pending final peer-reviewed journal publication.

scoreRationale.foundational: First open-source all-atom model unifying folding and cross-modal binder generation at atomic resolution.
scoreRationale.ripple: Broadly adopted across academic and biotech drug-discovery pipelines as an open alternative to closed commercial binder platforms.
scoreRationale.verification: Strong wet-lab experimental validation across nine novel targets and open code/weights, scored as Preprint / Active Review pending journal print.
scoreRationale.velocity: Achieved 66% target hit rates testing ~15 AI-designed candidates per target instead of screening millions of library clones.
